title: Frontend Mentor Challenges
description: Build real website components and pages from professional designs, then compare solutions with the community.

title: JavaScript30
description: Thirty small vanilla JavaScript projects in thirty days — no frameworks, no libraries, just the platform.

title: RealWorld Example App (Conduit)
description: Build a full Medium-style app against a real spec and API, in the frontend stack of your choice.

title: Publish a Personal Site with GitHub Pages
description: Ship your first live website: build a simple personal page and host it for free straight from a Git repository.

title: Flexbox Froggy
description: A game that tests your CSS flexbox skills level by level as you guide frogs to their lily pads.

title: CSS Diner
description: Interactive game testing your command of CSS selectors, from simple elements to advanced combinators.

title: W3Schools JavaScript Quiz
description: Quick 25-question quiz to check your grasp of JavaScript fundamentals.

title: Testing Library Documentation
description: Official guide to the Testing Library family (DOM, React, Vue): guiding principles, querying the DOM the way users do, firing events, async utilities and framework-specific setup. Teaches component testing that avoids implementation details.

title: Testing JavaScript
description: Eight video modules (about 9 hours) on testing JavaScript applications: testing fundamentals, mocking, static analysis, configuring Jest, DOM and React Testing Library, Cypress end-to-end tests and testing Node backends. Follows the static/unit/integration/e2e 'testing trophy' approach.

title: Redux Essentials, Part 1: Redux Overview and Concepts
description: The official eight-part Redux Essentials tutorial: core concepts, Redux Toolkit app structure, data flow, async logic and data fetching, performance and normalisation, then RTK Query basics and advanced patterns, built around a social-feed example app.

title: Guides | webpack
description: webpack's official guide series from Getting Started through asset and output management, development setup, code splitting, caching, tree shaking, environment variables, hot module replacement, TypeScript and production builds.

title: Digital Accessibility Foundations - Free Online Course
description: W3C WAI's self-paced course (delivered on edX) on what web accessibility is, how people with disabilities use technology, the business case, WCAG principles and standards, and first accessibility checks. About 16-20 hours over four modules.

title: Advanced React
description: Intermediate Meta course (about 26 hours) covering lists and forms, lifting state and the Context API, built-in and custom hooks, composition patterns such as higher-order components and render props, and testing components with React Testing Library, ending in a portfolio project.

title: Learn CSS
description: Google's 38-module evergreen CSS course: box model, selectors, cascade and specificity, flexbox, grid, logical properties, custom properties, transitions and animations, container queries, gradients, filters and blend modes, with self-check questions per module.

title: CSS Grid
description: Free 25-video course (about 4 hours) on CSS Grid: implicit and explicit tracks, sizing, item placement, minmax() and auto-fit responsive layouts, template areas, alignment, grid versus flexbox, and practical builds such as image galleries and a full responsive site.

title: Browser Rendering Optimization
description: Free six-lesson course by Paul Lewis and Cameron Pittman on the browser rendering pipeline: the critical rendering path, the RAIL model, finding and removing jank with Chrome DevTools, JavaScript and web-worker optimisation, style/layout costs and compositor layers.

title: Animations on the Web
description: Paid course by Emil Kowalski (Linear, ex-Vercel) on interface motion: animation theory (easing, timing, springs), CSS animations, Motion/Framer Motion from basics to complex sequences, what separates good from great animations, and four real-world walkthrough builds.
